Acceptance contract: Native PTY tabs handle input resize paste guard backpressure exit restart and reconnect
Current evidence: ISOLATED to the term.open command, and now classified for a host-owned session. Earlier work refuted total authority failure and a dead bridge: on the same host and session broker.status 10ms, files.list 31ms, settings.read 131ms, catalog.get 1509ms all answered while term.open threw at 30004ms, and files.list answered in 31ms at the moment the installed terminal claimed the connection had dropped, so that copy was false. The first host tracer was misplaced at DesktopOperationDispatcher and called ingress although server feature checks, confirmation, session loading, and observer barriers run earlier; the corrected trace emits received at server entry, server-returned or server-threw on settlement, operation-ingress at dispatcher entry, and authority-invoke or authority-ok around the authority. A new opt-in seeding control, --test-control gated on OMP_APP_TEST_MODE and refused on the default profile and on remote listeners, then created a disposable session that the candidate host both advertises and owns: seeded 1 indexed 1 with 70 durable entries, present in the host ownership ledger and in the wire inventory as T4 seeded elterm002 1. Running the production order against it, session.attach succeeded, sixty session.state.get calls over 15s returned session_locked, controller.lease.acquire returned session_locked, and term.open was refused in 0ms with session_locked while the host trace contained no term.open line at all, placing the refusal before host command entry at the observer barrier rather than in operation routing or the authority terminal lifecycle. The lock appears only after attach, names the host's own short-lived attach-spawned child, and is left behind stale when that child exits. Scope care, this is NOT proven to be the installed-app failure: the installed symptom waited 30s and reported a dropped connection while this refusal is immediate, so the installed timeout remains unexplained. Secondary findings, openTimeoutMs of 15s guards only post-acceptance correlation so users wait the client's 30s; backpressure pause fires but drain and input preservation remain unproven
Next proof: Establish whether the installed 30s timeout shares this pre-dispatch session_locked cause or is a distinct path, then fix the host treating its own attach-spawned child's lock as foreign and the stale lock that child leaves behind
